evidence: budgets.md's preamble claimed to be 'the single home for every number' and repeated nothing, then restated charter #3's two figures as 'Two owner directives'. The 6e9781c fix removed that section but its new sentence still spelled out 'under one second per command, held at 10x on both axes' (F16), and the '<1s directive' line in the harness bullet survived (F21).
guidance_note: When removing a restated figure from a doc, grep the whole file for every literal form of it ('1 second', '<1s', '10x') and rewrite each to a citation in the same commit, including the sentence you are writing yourself.

evidence: design.md's preamble says figures live in budgets.md, yet §cache said '(<1s, 10x fleet)' and §sync said 'eleven seconds' against budgets' 10.9 s row. The 6e9781c diff replaces both with citations.

The original ref-hygiene text required 'a sweep commit' with no author or ref named, which a dead checkout cannot write, so INV:single-writer-ref was unexplained. The fix specified the sweep, but it added a two-parent commit that contradicted §store's 'linear' claim (F14) and left the delete target and resurrection unspecified (F25).
guidance_note: When adding a mechanism to a design doc, reread every invariant and absolute claim it touches (here §store's 'linear chain' and 'nobody writes another's ref') and state where the new mechanism's effects land locally and remotely before pushing.

evidence: The order is (Lamport, writer-id), so for genuinely concurrent intents 'the later decision stands' is not recency. The 6e9781c diff narrows the claim to causally ordered intents and calls the concurrent case deterministic arbitration.

The row read 'negligible against a foreground command', the only non-numeric row in the Command table. The fix gave it numeric ceilings, but the same non-numeric shape in two Storage rows was left alone and came back as F17.
guidance_note: When a finding says one table row lacks a measurable threshold, check every row of every gated table for the same defect and fix them all in one commit.

evidence: The gate was 'every table in this file green', which included the descriptive baselines table and its 'unmeasured' rows. The 6e9781c bullet scopes the gate to the two budget tables.
The staleness row said 'runs at the top of every command', which left open whether its 20 ms adds to the <1 s ceiling. The fix states that command rows are inclusive totals.

The original text said only 'causal-position is a Lamport timestamp' and gave no advance-on-observe rule, so a deliberate override could sort before what it overrides. The fix stated the max+1 rule but did not say how it applies to the several events in one batched commit (F33).
guidance_note: When specifying a counter rule, state it at every granularity the doc defines (per event and per batched commit), because §store's 'one commit per command' was already on the page.

evidence: The quoted gate 'oracle diff empty and every table in this file green' differs from design's S1 row 'oracle diff empty over sustained real use; budgets pass at 10x'. The fix names design §migration as the owner and keeps 'sustained real use'.

The agent verified the gap: the child scheme maxChild+1 in internal/store/issue_ids.go collides under offline filing. The fix added an 'Issue identity' paragraph but deferred to access-control §1 as 'normative home', though that section said the opposite. This seeded F13/F19/F23 and the cascade after them, left the stale 'only id collisions surface' clause (F20), did not state that ordinals are unstable (F24), and left writer-id uniqueness unargued (F37).
guidance_note: Before writing that a second document is the 'normative home' for a rule, open that document and confirm it says the same thing; if it does not, amend it in the same commit or claim ownership here.

evidence: 'place X above Y' and a concurrent 'place Y above X' have different subjects yet do not commute, so the categorical commute claim was false. The 6e9781c fix narrows the claim to disjoint subject/anchor sets and forbids partitioning the fold by subject.

The general corpus definition implied 10x copies of the largest store, while the aggregate-disk row demanded a distribution-preserving fleet. The fix split the corpus into depth and breadth, but the breadth fleet stayed at 1x history (F15), the Command table was scoped to depth only (F31), and three Storage rows got no corpus (F34).
guidance_note: When introducing a definition that assigns rows to components, walk every row of every table and check that each one is assigned to a component that actually exercises the axes its label claims.

evidence: 6e9781c's Issue identity paragraph says it 'adopts the opaque-id direction the access-control design already mandates', but access-control §1 then still read 'Child .n suffixes may stay', which faedaae shows being removed. The F10 fix asserted an agreement with a document it did not update.
guidance_note: When a fix asserts agreement with another document, diff the claim against that document's text and amend it in the same commit.

evidence: 6e9781c added a sweep event 'with the dead ref's head as an additional git parent', a merge commit, while §store a few paragraphs up still said each ref is 'a linear, fast-forward-only chain'. faedaae qualifies that to first-parent linearity.
guidance_note: After adding a two-parent commit to a design, search the doc for 'linear', 'parent', and 'chain' and requalify each claim in the same commit.

evidence: 6e9781c defined the breadth fleet as '10x the measured store count, preserving the measured size distribution', i.e. 1x history per store, and pointed the 'at 10x both axes' aggregate row at it. faedaae adds 'with each store's history also scaled x10'.
guidance_note: When pointing a row at a newly defined corpus, check that the corpus scales every axis the row's label names.

evidence: The F1 plan promised budgets.md would 'stop restating' the directives and cite charter #3, yet the 6e9781c sentence reads 'The two governing directives — under one second per command, held at 10x on both axes — are charter.md hard constraint 3's'. The agent admitted 'the round-1 fix was partial'.
guidance_note: Reread your own replacement sentence against the plan you posted before pushing; a fix that removes a restatement must not write a new one.

evidence: The rows 'not measurable above noise' and 'pruned to live checkouts + anchored sweeps' are original text with the same non-numeric shape F5 fixed in the Command table. The F6 fix's 'every row of the two budget tables green' gate made them unautomatable gate rows.
guidance_note: When fixing one non-numeric row in a gated table, sweep every row of every gated table for the same defect.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the S2-S4 gate cells and charter #9's 'every advance is gated by the differential oracle agreeing and by budgets.md' are original text that 6e9781c did not touch, so the mismatch predates review. The premise holds, and the fix's new charter phrase 'through the write flip' then produced F27, while leaving S0 without a budgets clause produced F38.
guidance_note: When a design table instantiates a charter rule that says 'every X', check every row of the table against it in the original PR.

evidence: faedaae amended only access-control's child sentence, so §1 still described a title+description hash while event-store claimed §1 as the home of a (writer-id, causal-position, content) formula. dedf371 makes event-store the home of the mechanism for all ids.
guidance_note: When reconciling two documents' versions of one rule, compare every input of the rule, not only the clause the finding named.

evidence: 6e9781c declared ids 'impossible for two offline checkouts to collide on' but left §sync's 'only id collisions surface as fold advisories' unchanged, so the same file contradicted itself.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a property impossible, grep the doc for every sentence that still treats it as possible ('collision', 'collide') and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The 'Outlives the migration' bullet's 'so the <1s directive is enforced by the build' is pre-review text. Two fixes for F1/F16 rewrote the preamble to cite charter #3 and never swept this line in the same file; dedf371 replaces it with 'charter #3 directive'.
guidance_note: Removing a restated figure means grepping the file for every spelling of it ('<1s', 'one second'), not just editing the sentence the reviewer quoted.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the config-stream bullet's 'judges each event against its cited version' is original text faedaae did not touch. The finding itself is real, because cited-version judgment lets a revoked principal keep minting under an old permissive version. The agent took the reviewer's OPEN option and argued correctly that a receiver-knowledge rule would break deterministic folding.
guidance_note: When a design replaces a predecessor's serialized check (here the per-commit policy-version monotonicity in access-control Enforcement), state in the original draft how the new substrate preserves that property or mark it OPEN.

evidence: faedaae's new parenthetical delegated only the child mechanism, leaving §1's 'hash commitment to title+description' readable as the top-level formula. dedf371 marks that scheme 'retired' and moves minting for all ids to event-store. This is the same defect as F19, seen from the other document.
guidance_note: When splitting ownership between two documents, write the split explicitly in both in the same commit (policy here, mechanism there) and cover every case, not only the one the finding named.

evidence: 6e9781c/faedaae made .n ordinals 'fold-derived' over a Lamport order, and a late sibling with a lower counter can renumber its peers. The agent correctly rejected the reviewer's freeze-at-first-fold option ('machine-local state and would break INV:deterministic-fold') and took the reviewer's other option.
guidance_note: When a fix turns stored values into fold-derived ones, state in that fix whether the derived value is stable under late arrivals.

evidence: 6e9781c's sweep said only 'the dead ref is then deleted with a compare-and-swap', with no local/remote scope, while a background fetch would recreate a locally deleted ref. Its 'Nobody ever writes the dead ref' also conflicts with deleting it.
guidance_note: When specifying an operation on replicated state, state its effect on each replica and how the next sync interacts with it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the baseline rows '~1.1 GB' and '`du -sm` sum over the 57 dirs' are original text. The agent re-measured and confirmed the double-count: 901 MB deduplicated across 52 unique stores.
guidance_note: When a baseline row's own provenance admits double-counts, deduplicate before summing in the original measurement.

evidence: faedaae's new charter #9 wording 'for as long as the oracle exists, which is through the write flip' can be read to cover S3->S4, whose gate has no oracle clause. The reviewer admitted it was 'not fully certain which reading is intended', so this is an ambiguity rather than a defect. Stating the intent was the right move.
guidance_note: When adding a temporal qualifier like 'through X' to a charter rule, check it against each gate boundary in the table it governs.

evidence: dedf371 wrote 're-deletes a remote copy that reappears' and in the next sentence 'its next mirror push restores the ref', so a falsely swept live checkout would be silently excluded forever. 3aacb82 gates re-deletion on the anchor.
guidance_note: After writing a rule and an exception for it in the same paragraph, run the exception's scenario through the rule before pushing.

evidence: dedf371 made access-control §1 defer minting for every id to event-store §events, while access-control still framed itself as layers over the current Dolt store. That created an unacknowledged sequencing dependency, and 3aacb82 states it.
guidance_note: When a fix makes document A depend on mechanism in document B, check A's own framing of its substrate and sequencing and state the dependency in A.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the Adoption line 'fetch refs/lit/log/*' is original text, and dedf371 touched only the sentence after it. The inbox write path's dependence on an established clone's receive is a real gap in the original design.
guidance_note: When a design defines more than one ref namespace, check that every read path (receive, adoption) enumerates all of them.

evidence: The F12 fix in 6e9781c retitled the Command table 'at 10x depth corpus' and scoped per-command benchmarks to the single-store depth corpus, while charter #3 requires both axes. Command latency under breadth-fleet background load was therefore never exercised, and 3aacb82 adds that concurrent load.
guidance_note: When splitting a 'both axes' corpus into components, confirm that every charter requirement stated over both axes is still tested by some benchmark that has both.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the single signature-slot text and its 'changes policy, not schema' claim are original. The threshold-signature need comes from access-control's owner rotation. The agent's quorum-by-events fix dropped the new-owner leg, which led to F39.
guidance_note: When a birth-requirement slot is claimed sufficient for a future layer, check that layer's multi-party operations against it in the original draft.

evidence: 6e9781c's advance rule says 'a writer mints its next event at 1 + max(...)' without saying whether the several events in §store's one-commit-per-command batch each advance it. 3aacb82 states that the counter advances per event.
guidance_note: When stating an ordering rule, check it against every place in the doc where multiple events are produced at once.

evidence: The F12 fix's corpus definition named backers only for the Command rows and for aggregate disk and stampede. Per-store disk, git-experience latency, and dead-refs had no corpus until 3aacb82.
guidance_note: When introducing a row-to-corpus assignment, enumerate every row and give each an explicit corpus in the same commit.

evidence: 3aacb82's rule covers only 'at or behind' and 'past' the anchor. A checkout whose ref was deleted in a shared common dir would root a disjoint chain, which neither case covers, and it would be re-deleted. The fix in 3d8dc12 makes such a checkout resume from its anchor.
guidance_note: When writing a two-case classifier over refs, enumerate every relation a ref head can have to the anchor (behind, equal, ahead, unrelated) and handle each.

evidence: 3aacb82 tied the id redesign, and with it topic's move to an encryptable column, to the event-store migration. That made the unchanged shape paragraph's 'neither needs the other: ... the read layer alone meets the confidentiality bar' false for topic.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a sequencing dependency to one item, search the document for every 'independent' or 'alone' claim it now falsifies.

evidence: The F10 fix's 'impossible for two offline checkouts to collide on', strengthened by the F20 fix to cover never-connected workspaces, rests on writer-id uniqueness, which was never specified. The only nearby id is work-claims' short stream token. 3d8dc12 specifies a 128-bit token.
guidance_note: When writing an 'impossible' guarantee, list the inputs it depends on and confirm each one's uniqueness is specified somewhere.

evidence: The F18 fix added budgets clauses to S2-S4 but not S0, so the table narrowed charter #9's literal 'every advance'. The practical risk is minimal because S0 has nothing to benchmark, but the literal mismatch was created by a partial sweep.
guidance_note: When adding a clause to rows of a table to satisfy an 'every' rule, add it to every row or state the exception in the rule itself.

evidence: 3aacb82's 'activates at fold when the prior policy's threshold is met' omits access-control's requirement for 'signatures from a threshold of the old owners and the new'. The agent conceded: 'I dropped the dual-consent leg'.
guidance_note: When a fix implements a requirement from another document, quote that requirement verbatim into your plan and check every conjunct of it against the new text.

evidence: 3aacb82 justified deferring only id minting by citing 'the event-store charter's direction that the write layer's hardest machinery not be built against the substrate being retired'. That principle applies equally to §1's Dolt-based signing machinery, which carried no such caveat.
guidance_note: When citing a principle to justify a narrow exception, check whether the principle covers more of the document than the exception you are making.

narrative: This design-doc PR ran into the five-round cap with 40 findings, and the agent accepted every one. Almost all premises were correct, and in F24 the agent rightly rejected one of the reviewer's proposed cures. Rounds 1-3 each still raised some original-text findings (F18, F22, F26, F30, F32), but most findings in rounds 1-4 were caused by earlier fixes: claims asserted to agree with other documents that were not checked (F10->F13->F23->F29->F36/F40), new mechanisms that broke absolute claims elsewhere in the doc (F3->F14, F25->F28->F35), and partial sweeps of a defect class (F1->F16->F21, F5->F17, F12->F15/F31/F34). Every finding in round 4 traces to a prior fix, so rounds 4 and 5 were avoidable.
guidance_observations: Each fix was written as a narrow patch to the quoted sentence; the cascade came from not rereading the whole document, and the cross-referenced document, for claims the patch newly contradicted.

The agent repeatedly asserted cross-document agreement ('normative home', 'adopts the direction ... already mandates') without opening the other document, which cost three rounds on the issue-id thread alone.

Plans posted on threads were accurate, but the implemented text in 6e9781c did not match the F1 plan ('stop restating'). A check of each diff against its own posted plan before pushing would have caught it.

With round 5 capped and unreviewed, the fixes in 3d8dc12 (resume-from-anchor, 128-bit checkout id, dual-consent quorum, substrate note) merged with no review, which is the same shape that produced every prior round's fix-caused findings.
